newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 16.

text.p: South Korea's largest conglomerate group Samsung Co 78020.K plans to merge its electronics and trading house subsidiaries in Japan by the end of this year. It also plans to list shares of the new company, which is expected to have sales of more than 400 billion yen, on the second section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in four years.

The Hertz group, the world's largest rent-a-car company, will suspend the business of its loss-making Hertz Japan Co Ltd by the end of March. The parent company is looking for a buyer for the operation, but may liquidate the unit if the efforts prove unsuccessful. Hertz Japan is estimated to have had a net loss of 500 to 600 million yen in fiscal 1995/96, and has debts of between four to five billion yen.

NSK Ltd plans to start making car steering wheel components in India from 1998. It will set up a joint venture in cooperation with leading U.S. autoparts maker Torrington Co and Indian autoparts maker Rane (Madras) Ltd. The new company plans to make 500,000 steering wheels a year by 1999.

Mitsubishi Corp plans to set up a joint venture to make precipitated calcium carbonate, in cooperation with Minerals Technologies Inc and Tokyo-based chemical maker Fimatec Ltd. The new company is aiming for annual output of 200,000 to 400,000 tonnes by 2000.
